title: When to Sell an Off-Plan Contract: The 3 Moments That Raise Its Value
seoTitle: When to Sell an Off-Plan Contract: 3 Key Moments
description: Most off-plan buyers only think about when to buy. Learn the 3 construction moments that make your contract worth more and when to sell.
answer: The money in off-plan is made when you sell, not when you buy. Watch three moments: the crane goes up and construction starts, the building reaches its top floor, and a finished building nearby lets buyers compare prices. Each step makes the project more real, lowers the risk and makes your contract worth more. You do not need to wait for the keys.
body:
Most people who buy off-plan spend all their energy on one question: when should I buy? It is a fair question, but it is only half of the deal. In my experience, the money is made when you sell. If you do not have a plan for the exit, you are leaving the most important decision to chance.

## Why the value of an off-plan contract changes over time

When you buy off-plan, you are buying something that does not exist yet. The price reflects that risk. Every time the project takes a visible step forward, that risk shrinks, and buyers are willing to pay more for the same contract. You are not selling bricks. You are selling certainty, and certainty grows as the building becomes real.

## The 3 moments to watch

1. **The crane.** Construction starts. At this point the developer cannot go back. The biggest risk, that the project never gets built, drops. When the risk drops, the price goes up.
2. **The top floor.** The building reaches its full height. Now people can see it from the street. It is no longer a rendering or a promise. It is real, and buyers react to that.
3. **The finished building next door.** When a completed building nearby is on the market, buyers can compare. Your contract now has a reference point, a real price that people can check. That makes it easier to sell and easier to price.

## Every step that makes the building real adds value

The pattern is simple. Anything that makes the building more real makes your contract worth more. Construction starting, the structure rising, comparable buildings appearing around it. Each one removes a doubt from the next buyer's mind, and removing doubt is what people pay for.

## You do not have to wait for the keys

Many buyers assume they must hold until completion. That is one option, but it is not the only one. You can sell your contract at one of these moments, when the certainty has grown but you have not yet paid the full price of the unit. Before you do, check what your contract allows. Assignment rules and fees vary from project to project, and the timing only works if the contract lets you sell.

My view is simple: buy the risk early, and sell the certainty when the market can see it. Decide which of the three moments fits your plan before you sign, not after.
takeaways: The money in off-plan is made when you sell, not only when you buy.
When the crane goes up, the developer cannot go back, so risk drops and the price goes up.
When the building reaches its top floor, people can see it and it becomes real.
A finished building nearby gives buyers a real price to compare with your contract.
You do not have to wait for the keys; you can sell the certainty that construction creates.
faq: When is the best time to sell an off-plan property?

Many investors watch three moments: the start of construction, the building reaching its top floor, and a comparable finished building nearby. Each one lowers the risk for the next buyer and can raise the value of the contract.
Can I sell an off-plan property before completion?
In many projects you can assign or resell your contract before completion, but it depends on the terms of your purchase contract. Check the assignment rules and any fees before you plan your exit.
Why does an off-plan contract increase in value during construction?
As construction progresses, the risk that the building is not finished goes down. Buyers pay more for certainty, so the same contract becomes worth more.
